source_refs.note: Book p. 106: 6.8 A.G.P. definition (corresponding terms of an A.P. and a G.P. multiplied), general A.G.P. ab, (a+d)br, ... and its nth term {a+(n-1)d}br^(n-1)

blocks.text: Suppose \(a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_n, \ldots\) is an A.P., and \(b_1, b_2, b_3, \ldots, b_n, \ldots\) is a G.P. then the sequence formed by multiplying the corresponding terms of A.P. and G.P., that is, \(a_1b_1, a_2b_2, a_3b_3, \ldots, a_nb_n, \ldots\) is said to be an arithmetico-geometric sequence.
Consider an A.P., \(a, a + d, a + 2d, \ldots, \{a + (n - 1)d\}\) and a G.P., \(b, br, br^{2}, \ldots, br^{n-1}\) where \(r \ne 1\).

Multiplying the corresponding terms of A.P. and G.P., we get an arithmetico-geometric sequence
\[ab,\ (a + d)br,\ (a + 2d)br^{2},\]
\[\ldots,\ \{a + (n - 1)d\}br^{n-1}\]

The \(n\)th term of arithmetico-geometric sequence is product of \(n\)th term of A.P. and \(n\)th term of G.P. Thus, \(n\)th term of such sequence has the form
\[\{a + (n - 1)d\}br^{n-1}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
'Corresponding' means same position: 1st with 1st, 2nd with 2nd, and so on. In each A.G.P. term the 'coefficient' part (\(a, a + d, a + 2d, \ldots\)) grows by adding \(d\), while the 'power' part (\(b, br, br^{2}, \ldots\)) grows by multiplying by \(r\).
Why \(r \ne 1\)? If \(r = 1\) the G.P. is just \(b, b, b, \ldots\) and the product is an ordinary A.P. multiplied by \(b\), so nothing new happens.

blocks.caption: Building an A.G.P. term by term (our illustration)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: How to recognise an A.G.P.: split each term into two factors. In \(1\cdot 2 + 3\cdot 4 + 5\cdot 8 + \cdots\) the first factors \(1, 3, 5, \ldots\) are in A.P. (\(d = 2\)) and the second factors \(2, 4, 8, \ldots\) are in G.P. (\(r = 2\)). The \(n\)th term is then \((2n - 1)2^{n}\).

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. A.G.P.: multiply the A.P. and the G.P. term by term.
2. A.P. \(a, a + d, \ldots\) times G.P. \(b, br, \ldots\) gives \(ab, (a + d)br, (a + 2d)br^{2}, \ldots\)
3. \(n\)th term: \(\{a + (n - 1)d\}br^{n-1}\).
4. Both factors use the same position \(n\): \(a_nb_n\).

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Multiplying the \(n\)th A.P. term by the \((n+1)\)th G.P. term (power \(r^{n}\) instead of \(r^{n-1}\)).
2. Treating an A.G.P. as a G.P.: \(1, 4, 12, 32\) has no common ratio (\(4, 3, \frac{8}{3}\)).
3. Writing the A.P. term as \(a + nd\) instead of \(a + (n - 1)d\).
